note: The Java engine, which replayed 0.16.0 run for run up to 1.0.0; 1.1.0 changes only how the cost counts autoscaled parts and prices the peak (ADR-0074); 1.1.1 measures the base's per-request rates in the buckets nearest it when none is at it; 1.2.0 prices a third-party API without a price at its technology preset's price, or leaves it out of the month (ADR-0081); 1.2.1 counts a cache's refused lookups in its hit ratio and words the advice on a failing cache by what its callers lack (ADR-0082); 1.3.0 reports a database's busiest instance's CPU and sets its CPU ceiling where that instance fills (ADR-0083); 1.4.0 counts lost messages against availability and judges a message's age (ADR-0084); 1.5.0 sizes a Kafka broker from the Kafka experiment's measurements and reports idle consumers (ADR-0085); 1.5.1 counts a commit's log flush as a wait in the instant estimate, not as database CPU, which changes no simulated knee (ADR-0089); 1.5.2 spreads a cache's commands over every shard's cores in the instant estimate and counts a read-through cache's fills in its slots and CPU, which changes no simulated knee either (ADR-0092). Not frozen yet: its source trees (archsim-engine, archsim-model, archsim-cli) are pinned when it is frozen, before the next held-out campaign.

1.6.0 counts the vCPUs of a service, database or cache with 2 or more vCPU as hyperthread pairs at a sibling speed of 0.6 by default from schema 1.11, and as whole cores on an instance family whose vCPUs are whole cores, on a serverless platform and as pods on Kubernetes; auto-sizing sizes a part for the kind of vCPU its instance type gives it; and the instant estimate saturates a part on its own hyperthread pairs where its vCPUs fill at the sibling speed, at any load, and runs an overloaded one's work at that speed, where it extrapolated from the speed at the peak and, past its vCPUs, counted them taking turns at its own work too, and the design review judges such a part's CPU by the share of that ceiling its work takes, as the estimate does, and says so, where it judged it at the speed at the peak and called that share busy, so at 0.6 it said nothing from about 80% to 93% of the ceiling (ADR-0091). A design saved before 1.11, the benchmark harness's among them (schemas 1.0 and 1.7), is pinned to whole cores, so no simulated knee moves. It is counted as tuned on all nine experiments measured so far, the first held-out set's among them, since the change was made with their results in view; the second held-out set, registered before it (ADR-0090), stays held out. Not frozen yet: its source trees are pinned when it is frozen, before the next held-out campaign.
